Activity 2: Data Detective

Uncovering App Permissions & Tracking

Unit 2 Export to PDF Launch activity
Step 1

Launch MiniPhone OS

You have been given access to a simulated smartphone running MiniPhone OS. Your job is to investigate the apps installed on it and find out exactly what data they are trying to collect about you.

  • Open the simulation and go to the Messages app.
  • Follow the missions in the messages (one at a time).
  • On a laptop: use the Notes panel on the right for your checklist and “Impact” (on mobile: tap Notes).
Launch activity
Step 2

Create Your Investigation Log

Before you start, draw a simple table in your exercise book. You will fill it in as you explore each app.

Table headings

  • App
  • What data did it ask for?
  • Why might it want it?
  • What happens if you say NO?

Apps to investigate

  • Browser (cookies)
  • Connectify (terms & conditions)
  • MapMe (location)
  • Super Puzzle Quest (free app permissions)

Tip

  • Use short bullet points (no long paragraphs).
  • Use Case File and the Notes panel to see what data was collected.
Step 3

Complete the Missions

Follow the instructions in the Messages app. Work through one mission at a time. Keep notes in your investigation log. Use Case File to see what data was collected.

Browser (Cookies)

  • Try both: Accept all cookies and Essential only.
  • Tap a few items. Does the Sponsored section change?
  • What changes about the ads you see?
  • Use the cookie button to change your choice and try again.
  • Record what data might be collected if you accept all.

Connectify (Terms)

  • Tap the highlighted clauses in the Terms & Conditions.
  • Decide: would you agree or decline? Why?
  • If you agree: explore the tabs and look for “Sponsored” content.
  • Record what the app might do with your data.

MapMe (Location)

  • Try both: Precise and Approximate location.
  • Tap the pins on the map. Compare the dot vs the big circle.
  • Does the app still work without your exact location?
  • Use the crosshair button to change your location choice.
  • Record the privacy benefit of approximate location.

Super Puzzle Quest (Free app)

  • Notice what it asks for: tracking, camera, contacts.
  • After setup: watch one ad for coins. What do you notice?
  • What do you lose if you say NO?
  • Record why a “free” app might want your data.
Step 4

Reflection

A. The “greediest” app

Which app asked for the most data? Did it seem justified?

B. The trade-off

Give one example where you chose between privacy (keeping data safe) and convenience (making the app easier to use). What did you choose and why?

Step 5

Partner Discussion

Compare your “Data Footprint” score with your partner. Who has more items in their footprint? Why?

By the end of this task, you should be able to…

  • Identify common permissions apps ask for (location, photos, tracking)
  • Explain the trade-offs between privacy and functionality
  • Understand that “free” apps often pay for themselves with your data
  • Make informed choices about app permissions
